corrected_draft.title: Trump Issues Clemency Proclamation for January 6 Offenses
corrected_draft.description_short: On January 20, 2025, Trump issued a proclamation pardoning many people convicted of January 6 offenses, commuting named sentences and directing dismissal of pending indictments.
corrected_draft.description_medium: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump issued a clemency proclamation concerning offenses related to January 6, 2021. The proclamation granted pardons to certain defendants, commuted the sentences of named individuals, and directed the attorney general to dismiss pending indictments. It was not a Justice Department motion to vacate every conviction, and pardons or commutations are legally distinct from vacating convictions.
corrected_draft.description_long: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump issued a presidential proclamation addressing federal offenses related to events at or near the U.S. Capitol on January 6, 2021. The proclamation granted pardons to certain people convicted of those offenses, commuted the sentences of specifically named individuals to time served, and directed the attorney general to dismiss pending indictments. These actions were executive clemency. They were not a Department of Justice motion asking a court to vacate all January 6 convictions, and the proclamation did not describe every conviction as vacated. The proclamation commuted the sentences of 14 named defendants, including Stewart Rhodes and Joseph Biggs, to time served; it pardoned all other people convicted of offenses related to January 6. It directed the Bureau of Prisons to release those held in prison immediately and ordered the attorney general to pursue dismissal with prejudice of pending indictments. Those terms distinguish this presidential clemency action from a court motion to vacate convictions.
